findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. They can answer "what is it" and "why does it matter" before scrolling.
findings.source: Opening paragraph under the h1: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page lives at Athena's own address, but the title and most of the body are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets one short paragraph on it, then a long technical study of a tool they may never use.
findings.source: <title> and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: This is the second section on the page and the only place that would show Athena's promised trace of models, cost and verdict, but it shows an error message. A newcomer gets an internal failure where the proof should be, and that weakens trust in the claim made just above it.
findings.source: Section "Check it on a real job": "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link is meant for the project owner but sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. A first-time reader will not know whether it applies to them.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: where to read more, the clone command, prerequisites, the install script and a first command to try. The header links straight to this section, so "what to do next" is easy to find.
findings.source: Section "Next steps": "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The firstmate study is careful and every line has a citation, but it is dense: exit codes, guards, places-held and twelve transition cards. It shows that Athena can explain a codebase, but a newcomer has to read a lot to see that point, and the page never sums it up in one line.
findings.source: Sections "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions" (cards t1–t12)

findings.text: Several terms say only that the source does not define them. This is honest, but a newcomer is left with undefined words in the main walkthrough, for example "in scope" in the merge rule.
findings.source: Glossary entries such as "captain call": "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake, in scope)

findings.text: This is internal repository detail. It means nothing to a newcomer who has not cloned the repository.
findings.source: Section "About this page": "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
